## Why Devigner Icons

Two open icon sets, merged, deduplicated and consistently named, then built for
every framework below from one set of artwork. One design language, wherever
you work.

<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/devigner-ui/icons@main/.github/assets/features-dark.svg" />
  <img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/devigner-ui/icons@main/.github/assets/features-light.svg" width="100%" alt="12,480 drawings: 2,496 symbols on one 24×24 grid, every one free. Five styles each: outline, twotone, bold, bulk and broken. Every framework: React, Vue, Svelte, SolidJS, Angular, Nuxt, React Native, JavaScript, Flutter, Rails, Blazor and SVG. Search by meaning: one 384-dim vector per symbol ships as embeddings.json. TypeScript first: every symbol is a typed named export. Tree shakeable: sideEffects false, ship only what you import. No runtime dependencies: React 18 or later as a peer." />
</picture>

React needs 18+ and ships the `icons` CLI. Svelte covers 4 and 5, React Native
covers Expo, and Angular needs 16+. The Nuxt module auto-imports the Vue
package. Plain JavaScript gets SVG strings and elements, and the SVG package
covers everything else: CDN links, CSS and templates. The MCP server lets AI
coding tools search the set.

## Usage

```tsx
import { IconShoppingCart } from "@devigner-ui/icons/ShoppingCart";

export function CartButton() {
  return (
    <button>
      <IconShoppingCart className="size-5" />
      Checkout
    </button>
  );
}
```

Strokes are `currentColor`, so colour comes from CSS. Size the glyph with
`className`; the component has no `size` prop.

Importing the icon's subpath loads only that icon. It is the best choice for
dev servers, tests and tools that do not tree-shake:

```tsx
import { IconShoppingCart } from "@devigner-ui/icons/ShoppingCart";
import IconShoppingCart from "@devigner-ui/icons/ShoppingCart"; // same component
```

Named imports from the package root still work:

```tsx
import { IconShoppingCart } from "@devigner-ui/icons";
```

The ESM root re-exports individual modules, so production bundlers can remove
unused icons. The CommonJS root loads icon modules when their exports are
accessed. Plain Node, with no bundler, gets a single-file build of the root
instead of thousands of modules, so a server imports the whole set in a
fraction of a second. `sideEffects: false` tells bundlers these modules may be
removed when unused. Subpath types need
TypeScript's `moduleResolution` set to `"bundler"` or `"node16"`; the legacy
`"node"` setting cannot read subpath exports.

## Props

Three props of its own, **plus everything an `<svg>` takes** (`onClick`,
`style`, `id`, `width`, `fill`, `data-*`, the aria attributes) and a forwarded
`ref`.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | - | Sizes and colours the glyph. |
| `variant` | `"Outline" \| "TwoTone" \| "Bold" \| "Bulk" \| "Broken"` | `"Outline"` | Which drawing to render. Every icon has all five. |
| `strokeWidth` | `string \| number` | `"1.5"` | Stroke width, in the 24px drawing's own units. Outline, TwoTone and Broken; Bold and Bulk keep their own weight. |

Nothing is omitted from the inherited set any more: `width` and `fill` used to
be taken over for stroke width and which drawing, and are the element's own
attributes again. Size with `className` all the same: `width` sets one axis,
not both.

## Accessibility

Icons are **decorative by default** (`aria-hidden="true"` and
`focusable="false"`) because an icon sitting next to its own text label is
otherwise announced twice.

```tsx
<button>
  <IconTrash className="size-4" />   {/* hidden; the word "Delete" is the label */}
  Delete
</button>
```

Give it an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` and it becomes an image instead:
`role="img"`, no longer hidden.

```tsx
<button onClick={remove}>
  <IconTrash aria-label="Delete" className="size-4" />
</button>
```

## Refs

Every icon forwards its ref to the `<svg>`, so it works as a Radix or Headless
UI trigger and anything else that needs to measure or position against it.

```tsx
<Tooltip.Trigger asChild>
  <IconInfo aria-label="More information" />
</Tooltip.Trigger>
```

## Styles

`variant` selects one of the five drawings:

```tsx
<IconShoppingCart />                       {/* outline, the default */}
<IconShoppingCart variant="TwoTone" />
<IconShoppingCart variant="Bold" />
<IconShoppingCart variant="Bulk" />
<IconShoppingCart variant="Broken" />
```

If an app uses one style throughout, import from that style's entry instead.
Each icon then ships one drawing rather than all five, roughly a third of the
bytes:

```tsx
import { IconShoppingCart } from "@devigner-ui/icons/bold";
import IconShoppingCart from "@devigner-ui/icons/bold/ShoppingCart"; // one icon

<IconShoppingCart className="size-5" />    {/* always Bold */}
```

The entries are `outline`, `twotone`, `bold`, `bulk` and `broken`. A
component from one of them always draws that style and ignores `variant`;
every other prop works the same. Entries can be mixed in one app.

**All five styles are free on all 2,496 symbols**, and this package contains
every drawing.

```ts
import metadata from "@devigner-ui/icons/metadata.json";

const cart = metadata.icons.find((i) => i.name === "ShoppingCart");
cart.freeStyles; // ["outline", "twotone", "bold", "bulk", "broken"] when supplied
cart.proStyles;  // []
```

## CLI

This package ships one executable, `icons`, with no dependencies of its own:

```bash
npx @devigner-ui/icons search "upload progress"
npx @devigner-ui/icons copy ShoppingCart --format=svg
npx @devigner-ui/icons list --category=shopping-ecommerce
npx @devigner-ui/icons info ShoppingCart
```

`search` ranks against the shipped `embeddings.json`. Embedding the query needs
`@xenova/transformers`, which is not a dependency; without it, search falls
back to keyword matching and says so. `--keyword` asks for that directly.

`copy --format=svg` renders the installed React component rather than keeping a
second copy of the artwork, so the two cannot drift apart.

## Renamed icons

3.5.0 named variants for what they draw (`IconBag2` is now
`IconBagStraps`), corrected names the drawing didn't match (`IconNotebook`
is now `IconLaptop`), fixed spelling and capitalisation (`IconMagnifer` is
now `IconMagnifier`), and pointed 50 duplicate icons at the icon they
copied (`IconPlusCircle` renders `IconAddCircle`): 654 names in all. The
old names keep working until 4.0.0: your editor marks
them deprecated, and development builds log the new name once. To update a
project in one step:

```bash
npx @devigner-ui/icons migrate --dry   # list what would change
npx @devigner-ui/icons migrate
```

Every rename is listed in `@devigner-ui/icons/renames.json`. See
[Renamed icons](https://icons.devigner.cc/docs/guide/renamed-icons/).

## Exports

ESM and CJS builds, one subpath per icon (`./ShoppingCart`), one entry per
style (`./bold`, and `./bold/ShoppingCart` per icon), plus `./metadata.json`,
`./embeddings.json`, `./renames.json` and `./styles.css` subpath exports. `IconName`, `IconStyle`,
`IconProps` and `IconComponentType` are exported; `IconName` is a literal union
of all 2,496 symbol names.

`embeddings.json` holds one 384-dimension vector per icon, produced with
`Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, for ranking icons against a description.
